directAnswer: Pope Marinus II reigned from 942 to 946, chosen under the authority of Alberic II, the lay ruler of Rome. His pontificate was quiet and focused on church administration; medieval scribes later confused his name, listing him as Martin III.

paras: Marinus was a Roman cleric elected in late October 942. Like the popes immediately before him, he owed his election to Alberic II, who controlled every appointment of consequence in Rome. The sources suggest he accepted this arrangement and did not attempt to challenge Alberic's authority in civil matters.

The documents from his reign concern privileges for monasteries and churches, including grants supporting the reform movement that Alberic and Odo of Cluny had encouraged in Rome. He also dealt with ordinary questions of church discipline. Nothing dramatic is recorded of his three and a half years, and the Liber Pontificalis offers only brief notes. He died in the spring of 946.

Medieval copyists sometimes read the abbreviated names of Marinus I and Marinus II as Martin, and the two popes were listed as Martin II and Martin III. When Simon de Brion became pope in 1281, he took the name Martin IV, accepting that faulty count. In reality only one earlier pope, Martin I, had borne the name.

keyFacts: Roman cleric elected under Alberic II
Granted privileges to monasteries and churches
Misidentified in medieval lists as Martin III
The error explains why the 1281 pope became Martin IV

faqs.question: Why was Marinus II called Martin III?
faqs.answer: Medieval scribes misread the names of Marinus I and II as Martin, so both were mistakenly counted among the popes named Martin.

faqs.question: Did Marinus II have political power in Rome?
faqs.answer: No. Alberic II controlled Rome's government, and Marinus confined himself largely to church administration.
